transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-22
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park, Samir Gupta, Riley Cho (Redwood); Marta Lopez, Raj Patel, Evan Kim, Priya Shah, Tom Alvarez (Aegis)

Summary: quick closure workshop after the May 18th service degradation that affected token generation latency and triggered fallback. Focus was on root cause, mitigations (patch & config), and next steps for private deployment and Reserved capacity customers.

Topics: incident timeline, KV cache eviction hypothesis, prefix caching and long-tail tokens, reserved capacity vs burst, private VPC patch plan, SOC2/security questions, rollout schedule.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Lena Park: okay hi everyone thanks for joining on short notice, um we'll try to run through timeline, fixes, and a clear handoff. Marta, do you want to kick off with the customer impact summary?
[00:18] Marta Lopez: yeah thanks Lena, so on Monday the 18th at ~09:12 local we saw a spike in 5xxs and latency, um about 17% of requests saw token delays beyond 3s, a small percent fell back to slower model, and some client sessions timed out. It affected two production routes, the recommender and the chat multimodal.
[00:40] Lena Park: got it. Samir, quick recap from our side on what the runtime observed?
[00:45] Samir Gupta: sure so our telemetry shows a burst of mem pressure on a subset of GPUs leading to aggressive KV cache evictions, which then increased recompute and caused cold cache penalty. There's also a small bug in the prefix cache index that could over-count when there are multiple near-identical requests — we call it the "prefix zipper" heur. sorry thats a terrible name i just made up.
[01:10] Raj Patel: to confirm, the eviction was on dedicated nodes or shared?
[01:13] Samir Gupta: in your case the cluster was running Redwood Private on prem with mixed-instance pools. The affected workers were on an older cuda driver and we saw a kernel fallback that reduced memory eff, so evictions started sooner.
[01:30] Evan Kim: and the recommender route has lots of longer contexts yeah, so cold cache hit is expensive.
[01:35] Lena Park: right. There was also a compaction job around 09:05 that increased IO — combined with driver fallback it amplified pressure.
[01:44] Tom Alvarez: that compaction was an internal daily job from Aegis, we can reschedule.
[01:48] Priya Shah: security angle — any data exfil or PII exposure from cache evictions?
[01:52] Samir Gupta: we checked audit logs and KV cache eviction doesn't persist out of process — it's volatile in memory. No evidence of exfil. We did capture traces showing the eviction calls but nothing written to disk.
[02:06] Priya Shah: good, we'll want that in writing for our SOC 2 reviewer.
[02:10] Riley Cho: noted, we'll put together a short security addendum.
[02:13] Marta Lopez: curious about the driver fallback bit, is that from Redwood runtime selecting different kernels?
[02:18] Samir Gupta: yes, when we detect the older driver we sometimes fall back to slower kernels that are memory-inefficient. Our newer kernels rely on a CUDA 12+ optimization; older drivers force a compatibility path.
[02:30] Raj Patel: why didn't the autoscaler spin up more nodes? We saw queueing.
[02:34] Samir Gupta: autoscale triggered but the provisioning for on-prem took longer due to the compaction IO spike causing host-level I/O contention. Also some of the reserved pools were at cap — your config pins a minimum but burst capacity was limited.
[02:50] Marta Lopez: we had reserved capacity for daytime but underestimated peak footprints, and we were on mixed generations to save cost.
[02:56] Lena Park: ok that aligns — main root causes: driver mismatch causing kernel fallback -> increased mem footprint -> KV cache thrash; compaction job + limited burst capacity -> slower provisioning; prefix cache index bug aggravated similar requests.
[03:15] Evan Kim: what's the fix surface? software patch? config? capacity?
[03:19] Samir Gupta: three parts: 1) runtime patch to fix prefix indexing and reduce over-counting, 2) kernel advisory — upgrade drivers or opt into gpus with newer cuda, 3) autoscale/backoff tuning and temporary mitigation: increase KV cache soft limits and enable a smoothing window for compaction IO.
[03:40] Lena Park: Samir, can you elaborate the patch risk?
[03:43] Samir Gupta: patch is low risk; it's a correctness fix in the prefix cache codepath. We'll ship a builds with tests and a canary on non-critical routes. Private customers get a downloadable package and manual install steps, hosted customers get a fast rollout. We will also include a fallback policy to route to a smaller model gracefully if cold cache persists.
[04:05] Tom Alvarez: for Aegis Private we'd prefer a manual patch install rather than auto-upgrade.
[04:09] Samir Gupta: totally fine, we'll provide the package and a step-by-step.
[04:12] Raj Patel: one more question — KMS rotations? Our security says we want KMS rotation after the incident. Any impact?
[04:18] Lena Park: none from the eviction; keys are separate. But Samir can confirm if any runtime restarts are needed.
[04:25] Samir Gupta: KMS rotation is orthogonal; no rekeying required for the patch. We'll confirm the sequence in the install doc.
[04:33] Priya Shah: please include SAML/SSO verification steps for the private console in the checklist.
[04:38] Riley Cho: will do.
[04:40] Marta Lopez: ok, timeline for patch and verification?
[04:43] Samir Gupta: we're targeting an internal canary by 2026-05-24, a private package ready by 2026-05-26, and a hosted gradual rollout the week after. For Aegis, manual install and validation ideally by 2026-05-29.
[04:58] Lena Park: noted. Also we need to agree on SLA credit and a short term capacity burst for you while you validate the patch. Legal is in copy and we'll send a proposed credit calc.
[05:09] Tom Alvarez: appreciate that.
[05:11] Marta Lopez: what about longer term — should we move more routes to dedicated reserved gen-3?
[05:17] Samir Gupta: we recommend pinning heavy long-context routes to newer gen GPUs or enabling higher soft reservations; Redwood Optimize can run a batching/quantization suggestion to reduce token cost.
[05:27] Evan Kim: will those changes change output quality? We're sensitive about recommender precision.
[05:31] Lena Park: Optimize recommendations include quality regress checks — we can run AB evals on your seed prompts before changing quantization.
[05:37] Raj Patel: ok please add the AB test plan in the pilot scope.
[05:40] Lena Park: will do.
[05:41] Priya Shah: anybody from Redwood have a security pack link?
[05:44] Riley Cho: yes i'll drop the SOC2, architecture diagram, and the KMS notes into the shared folder after this call.
[05:50] Marta Lopez: thanks. A quick note, we did capture partial traces and have a sample session that hit the fallback. If you want we can share it, it's sanitized.
[05:58] Samir Gupta: please do, that'll help validate the patch against your exact pattern.
[06:02] Marta Lopez: we'll upload by EOD.
[06:05] Lena Park: okay, to recap next steps: Samir to deliver patch package & install steps, Lena to share compact RCA + proposed SLA credit calc, Riley to upload security docs, customer to upload traces + logs and run local replay, and schedule validation call week of 2026-05-31. Anything else?
[06:24] Tom Alvarez: can we also get a checklist for the mitigation toggles to temporarily reduce cold cache effect? like soft limit changes?
[06:31] Samir Gupta: yes we'll include temporary knobs: increase soft cache limit, enable cache smoothing window, and disable compaction during peak windows.
[06:40] Priya Shah: and we need the manual install verification steps for SSO and KMS listed explicitly.
[06:46] Riley Cho: will add.
[06:48] Evan Kim: last thing, who owns the postmortem writeup?
[06:52] Lena Park: Samir and Lena will co-author, then send a compact version for your SOC reviewer.
[06:57] Marta Lopez: great thanks all.
[07:00] Lena Park: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via the shared drive and calendar invite.

End of transcript.

References/Artifacts shared in call:
- Link: compact RCA doc (placeholder) -> will be shared after call
- Link: patch package (private s3 link) -> to be delivered by Samir
- Link: SOC2 extract + architecture diagram -> Riley to upload
- Trace samples uploaded by Aegis (link placeholder)

Notes on transcription: some product names transcribed inconsistently (prefix cache index referred to as "prefix zipper" in the call), speaker labeling approximate in a few cross-talk segments.
